subject: FastBank: multi-region activation SLA — scope & carveout clarification
messages:
From: Mark Holden <mark.holden@fastbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@fastbank.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA for multi-region activation and RTO/RPO expectations

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked great. We have an internal kickoff with our infrastructure and compliance teams next week and they pushed back on two items in the standard SLA that we need clarity on before we can proceed:

1) Recovery Time Objective (RTO): FastBank requires a guaranteed regional failover time not to exceed 15 minutes end-to-end (detection -> traffic cutover -> session rehydration).
2) Recovery Point Objective (RPO): We need confirmation of the maximum data-loss window during region switchovers (persistent KV caches and request logs).

Given Redwood’s multi-deployment model, can you confirm if these are supported as a contract-level commitment, and if not, what an exception plan or carveout would look like (pricing, warm-standby configuration, runbook attachment, and any conditions that would void the commitment)?

We'd also like to understand the fallback behavior if the primary region is degraded but still partially serving traffic — do you do traffic weighting before a full switchover or immediate cutover?

Appreciate a clear write-up we can bring to our risk committee. CCing Priya (Infra lead) who will coordinate technical questions.

Thanks,
Mark
Mark Holden
VP, Platform Engineering — FastBank

Subject: Re: SLA for multi-region activation and RTO/RPO expectations

Hi Mark (and Priya),

Thanks — great questions and it's good to align early. Short answer up front: we can support a documented multi-region activation commitment, but it requires a jointly-agreed scope (warm-standby cadence, replication guarantees, and runbook acceptance) plus an associated capacity reservation. Below I sketch a pragmatic exception path so your committee can evaluate cost versus risk.

Scope we typically require for a hard RTO <= 15m / RPO <= 1m:
- Dedicated warm-standby in a secondary region with pre-provisioned GPU pool and KV synchronization (continuous replication with transactional acknowledgements).
- Prefix and KV cache warming using recent traffic replay and proactive KV prefetch for session rehydration.
- Proactive synthetic monitors and automated failover runbook that Rishi's team will sign off on.

Operational caveats and constraints:
- The commitment applies only to planned and unplanned region outages that meet our availability criteria (we exclude severe cross-region networking partitions and operator-caused configuration changes).
- Third-party dependencies (customer-managed upstream services) are out of scope for the RTO/RPO guarantee.
- We require a monthly dedicated capacity reservation (minimum 2x your steady-state burst) while the carveout is active.

Fallback behavior options (choose one for contract):
A) Weighted traffic ramp: we shift traffic gradually to the standby and perform a rolling session rehydration (lower risk of cache storms, slightly longer overall duration).
B) Immediate cutover: full traffic redirect to standby after automated health checks (lower latency for decision but higher chance of transient errors during rehydration).

Attached is a draft SLA proposal (SLA_Draft_Proposal_v2.pdf) and some internal metrics from similar customers (DR_RTO_RPO_Metrics.xlsx) that show observed warm-standby activation times at different pre-warm levels.

If you'll share the committee calendar I can join to walk through the tech assumptions. Typical next steps: you pick fallback option A or B, we map the scope, legal reviews an addendum, and we lock the capacity commitment.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: FastBank: multi-region activation SLA — scope & carveout clarification

Rishi / Neha — forwarding FastBank's ask. TL;DR: they want a contract-level RTO <=15m, RPO <=1m. I proposed a dedicated warm-standby with continuous KV replication and two fallback behaviors (weighted vs immediate). See attachments.

Engineering asks (Rishi) — can we confirm the practical activation numbers if we: a) reserve 2x capacity in standby, b) pre-warm prefix caches with last-6h traffic replay, c) enable transactional KV replication? Please quantify median and 95th percentile activation time for our current runtime (A100/RTX clusters) and call out any edge cases (large KV blobs, model-level cold starts).

Legal asks (Neha) — what standard carveouts should we propose for network partitions and customer third-party services? Also need a short template for an addendum that ties SLA to capacity reservation and a monthly fee.

I will propose Option A (weighted ramp) as default unless you push back — it's lower risk for FastBank's sessions.

Thanks,
Grace

Subject: Re: FastBank: multi-region activation SLA — scope & carveout clarification

Grace / Neha / Mark / Priya — quick engineering readout after tabletop and a short test run with the perf lab yesterday. Key items: 

1) Activation times (lab, 95th pct):
- With 2x reserved standby + prefix replay (last 6 hours): median activation 7m, 95th 13m.
- With 1.25x reserved standby (cost-saving option): median 13m, 95th 24m (misses the 15m target).

2) RPO behavior:
- Transactional KV replication achieves sub-30s tail for writes under normal load. However, large bulk writes (>50MB per key) can extend catch-up window. We will set a per-key size guardrail in the addendum.

3) Failure modes and mitigation:
- Cross-region network partitions where replication stalls: those are guarded by an automated quorum check and will fall into the carveout.
- Operator-driven configuration changes that alter routing: carveout.

4) Recommendation for contract:
- Accept Option A (weighted traffic ramp) as Redwood default. Benefits: smoother session rehydration and lower risk of 5xx spikes.
- Commit to 2x standby reservation while the carveout is in effect. Quarterly review to adjust the multiplier based on observed traffic.

Neha, legal template notes: include explicit exclusion language for cross-region networking partitions, clear definition of what constitutes a regional outage, and tie the guarantee to an active capacity reservation (monthly invoice).

Mark / Priya — if this is acceptable we can spin the addendum and a DocuSign envelope. I attached the draft metrics and I'll follow up with a short runbook excerpt that we want them to accept.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
